title: Blood Orange Sherbet
changes_from_base: Blood orange juice and zest replace the orange and lemon; the cream is whisked straight in rather than whipped, and more corn syrup keeps it soft.
summary: No cooking at all: blood orange juice and zest whisked with cream and sugar for a creamy, rosy sherbet.

ingredients.item: blood orange juice, strained (from about 12 oranges), chilled
light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Zest and juice
steps.text: Grate the zest from two oranges first, then squeeze them all and strain the juice.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the juice, zest, cream, corn syrup and sugar together in the bowl until you can no longer feel sugar grains on the base.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Whisk in the salt, taste and add a pinch more if it needs lifting.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: If the oranges were at room temperature, refrigerate the mix for 2-3 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn for 20-30 min; eat it soft or freeze for 4 h for firmer scoops.

tips: Chill the oranges before juicing and you can churn straight away.
Corn syrup keeps the sherbet soft enough to scoop straight from the freezer.
Ordinary oranges work too; the colour will be paler.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper on the surface in the freezer for up to 1 week. Soften for 5-10 min before scooping.
